segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
approaching an intersection
shall yield
the right-of-way
to a vehicle which has entered the intersection
from a different highway.
Except as otherwise provided in subsection 4 [NRS-484B-250-4],
this section does not apply at intersections controlled by official traffic-control devices
or to vehicles approaching each other from opposite directions,
when the driver of one of the vehicles is intending to
or is making a left turn.

elements.justification: The driver of a vehicle: the vehicle aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); the driver role read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Approaching an intersection is occupying a carrier whose entrance end is that intersection: rel.occupies on a carrier c (st.travel_region) with st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'; 'a road user occupying one such carrier approaches through it whatever its motion'. Not the subject's presence in the intersection, which the obligation reads.

Yielding is not moving into the intersection (drv.motion.moving with rel.occupies of st.intersection) while the precedence of another vehicle is owed; the entry observation, where x's footprint overlaps both c and i, is where it is judged.

A vehicle y (vehicle aggregate) which has entered: y's footprint overlaps i (rel.occupies) and has overlapped it continuously since an observation at which y occupied a carrier cy with st.lane_enters cy i, the carrier it entered from.

From a different highway: y's carrier cy lies on a st.highway ('the entire public way between its boundary lines') (st.on_way 'the public way ... a structure region lies on') that x's approach carrier c does not lie on.

An official traffic-control device (DEF-NRS-484A-145 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority') that controls an intersection: the words 'intersections controlled by' limit its members to the devices that assign precedence at the junction - dev.traffic_signal 'a signal head', dev.stop_sign 'regulatory sign requiring a full halt', dev.yield_sign 'regulatory sign requiring yielding' - that govern i or a carrier entering it (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection'). Markings, warning and guide signs control no precedence at the junction and are left out. Official status read from presence.

Vehicles (aggregate) approaching from opposite directions: rel.oncoming's contract says the direction a road user approaches from is 'read through the carrier it approaches through ... and through that carrier's direction (st.lane_direction)'. x's approach carrier c and y's approach carrier cy (each with st.lane_enters into i, y's being the one it entered from) have designated directions (st.lane_direction 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in') whose dot product is below minus p.opposed_approach_cos_tolerance.

Is making a left turn: the vehicle's heading is turning to the left (drv.motion.turning_left, yaw rate to the left above the resolution) while its footprint overlaps the intersection (rel.occupies, st.intersection).

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash')
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash between x and y is a predicted closest approach of their centres, under constant velocities (which carry direction, speed and proximity), within the time-to-collision horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below the clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

applicability: x is a vehicle. Judged at each observation at which x occupies a carrier c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is an intersection i (st.lane_enters c i) - x approaching i, the observation of its entry, where its footprint overlaps both c and i, included - and there is a vehicle y other than x that has entered i from a different highway: y's footprint overlaps i and has overlapped it continuously since an observation at which y occupied a carrier cy with st.lane_enters cy i, cy lying on a highway (st.on_way) that c does not lie on. A y is not counted (exception) where x and y approach from opposite directions (dot product of st.lane_direction of c and cy below minus p.opposed_approach_cos_tolerance) and x or y has a declared intention to turn left at i (int.turn_left) or is turning left within i (drv.motion.turning_left with p.yaw_rate_tolerance). Not applicable where i is controlled by an official traffic-control device: a traffic signal, stop sign or yield sign governs i or a carrier whose entrance end is i (dev.governs); this exception is suspended where NRS_484B_250_4_o1 or NRS_484B_250_4_o2 applies to x (an intersection whose signal is inoperative when x enters).
obligation: At a judged observation at which x's footprint overlaps i and x is moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance), no vehicle y of the applicability (bound again with its whole selection and exception) has its centre and x's approach within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
The official status of a signal or sign is read from its presence on the road.
Yielding is judged where x moves into or within the intersection; slowing on the approach before entry is not separately checked.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: No device governs i or its approaches. x approaches on lane c (st.lane_enters c i, on highway A); y entered i from lane cy on highway B and is crossing. x moves into i; predicted closest approach 1 m in 1.5 s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same, but x halts on c while y crosses i and enters only after y has left.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A dev.stop_sign governs c; the intersection is controlled by an official device and no signal is inoperative.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but st.lane_enters is not observed, so whether x approaches i and from which carrier y entered is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x and y approach on opposed carriers (dot product of directions -1); y has int.turn_left at i and is turning left within i when x moves in: y is excepted and no other vehicle has entered i.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: i is governed by a dev.traffic_signal that is dev.inoperative at x's entry; the device exception is suspended; y crossing from highway B, conflict predicted when x moves in.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: x approaches and enters an uncontrolled intersection with no other road user in the scene.

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red with a green turn arrow:
Except as otherwise provided in paragraph (b) [NRS-484B-307-9b],
vehicular traffic
facing the signal
may enter the intersection only to make the movement indicated by the green turn arrow,
but must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.
Drivers turning in the direction of the arrow are thereby advised that so long as the turn arrow is illuminated, oncoming or opposing traffic simultaneously faces a steady red signal.

elements.justification: The signal is a dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {..., circular_red, green_arrow(dir), ...}; several states may be displayed at once': a steady red with a green turn arrow is circular_red displayed with green_arrow(dir), dir left, right or u_turn (a turn arrow); circular_red is the steady red, flashing_red a separate state. The signal governs (dev.governs) the approach carrier (st.travel_region, rel.occupies) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters), or the intersection (st.intersection) itself. Read at the entry into the intersection, the event the words fix it to ('may enter').

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel'). The law's own qualifier 'vehicular' limits the members the duty reads to those travelling by vehicle or conveyance: it leaves out pedestrians, read by the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian as a condition beside the traffic aggregate (x is not a pedestrian), and ridden or herded animals, which no road-user class of the ontology carries. Bicycles and the other conveyances stay in, as paragraph (b), which the words except, confirms by naming them.

Facing the signal: the signal governs the approach carrier x occupies at the observation before its entry whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters, dev.governs, rel.occupies), or the intersection itself; the heading is not read, as st.lane_enters states.

Entering the intersection is the rise of x's overlap with it (rel.occupies, st.intersection); the movement made through it is recognized at the exit: drv.motion.left_turn_through_region(x, i), drv.motion.right_turn_through_region(x, i) or drv.motion.straight_through_region(x, i), each from the heading change since entry integrated from kin.yaw_rate. The movement indicated by the green turn arrow is the one matching the green_arrow(dir) displayed (dev.traffic_signal) at the entry: left for green_arrow(left), right for green_arrow(right), through for green_arrow(straight).

residues.why: An advisory statement of the signal phasing (opposing traffic faces a steady red while the arrow is lit); it permits, requires and forbids nothing, and no duty of the road user turns on it.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and not of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian; at the judged observation x leaves an intersection i; at x's entry into i (the observation at which its overlap with i last became true, read through a past operator) a traffic signal s governing the approach carrier c x occupied at the observation before the entry (dev.governs(s, c) with st.lane_enters(c, i), or dev.governs(s, i)) displayed circular_red together with at least one green_arrow(dir). The duty does not apply where a node of paragraph (b) applies (NRS_484B_307_9b_o1 to _o4, ruleApplies with x mapped to x).
obligation: The crossing x completes is the movement an arrow s displayed at the entry indicates: violated where it is drv.motion.left_turn_through_region(x, i) and s displayed no green_arrow(left) at the entry, drv.motion.right_turn_through_region(x, i) and no green_arrow(right), or drv.motion.straight_through_region(x, i) and no green_arrow(straight); step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, angles p.straight_through_max_heading_change, p.left_turn_min_angle, p.right_turn_min_angle, p.reversal_min_angle. The signal is read at the entry through a past operator from the exit, where the act is recognized.

narrowings.why: 'only to make the movement' states the purpose of the entry; it is read through the movement made through the intersection, recognized at the exit.

The movements judged are a left turn, a right turn and a through movement; a crossing none of the three concepts classes (a heading change between the through and the turn bounds, or a reversal) is not judged a breach. The trigger and condition spans are read at the entry, which the formula reaches from the exit, the act's recognition, through a past operator.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car on an approach lane governed by a signal showing circular_red with green_arrow(left) enters the intersection and leaves it with a heading change below the straight-through bound.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same car enters on circular_red with green_arrow(left) and leaves with a left turn.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The car enters on circular_green and goes straight through.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car enters on circular_red with green_arrow(left) and leaves the intersection; the source supplies no yaw rate, so the movement made is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle enters on circular_red with green_arrow(left) and goes straight through: paragraph (b) applies to it, so this duty does not.

onset.justification: Each act's record declares its beginning at the entry, the observation at which the road user's overlap with the intersection (rel.occupies, st.intersection) last became true.

occasion.recognition: The act is recognized at the observation it leaves the region.

under_way.words: enter the intersection only to make the movement
under_way.justification: An observation inside the act is one at which x, having entered, still overlaps the intersection and is in motion (drv.motion.moving, reading kin.speed); before the entry it did not overlap it.

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red with a green turn arrow:
Except as otherwise provided in paragraph (b) [NRS-484B-307-9b],
vehicular traffic
facing the signal
may enter the intersection only to make the movement indicated by the green turn arrow,
but must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.
Drivers turning in the direction of the arrow are thereby advised that so long as the turn arrow is illuminated, oncoming or opposing traffic simultaneously faces a steady red signal.

elements.justification: The signal is a dev.traffic_signal, 'several states may be displayed at once': circular_red displayed with green_arrow(dir), governing (dev.governs) the approach carrier (st.travel_region, rel.occupies) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters), or the intersection (st.intersection); read at the entry, the event the words fix it to.

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ...'); the qualifier 'vehicular' leaves out pedestrians, read by the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian as a condition beside it (x is not a pedestrian), and ridden or herded animals, which no class atom carries.

Facing the signal: the signal governs the approach carrier x occupies at the observation before its entry whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters, dev.governs, rel.occupies), or the intersection itself.

Yielding the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: the other's right 'to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another ... approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash') is read as x, while moving (drv.motion.moving) in the intersection, never standing in a predicted conflict with the parties: prim.closest_approach_within over the conflict horizon with prim.closest_approach_distance below the conflict clearance. Pedestrians are the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian occupying (rel.occupies) an adjacent crosswalk, a st.crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance (st.entrance_of) of a carrier (st.travel_region) that enters the intersection (st.lane_enters); other traffic is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, other than x, occupying the intersection (st.intersection).

residues.why: An advisory statement of the signal phasing (opposing traffic faces a steady red while the arrow is lit); it permits, requires and forbids nothing, and no duty of the road user turns on it.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and not of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian; at the judged observation x occupies an intersection i and has occupied it at every observation since its entry (the rise of its overlap with i), and at that entry a traffic signal s governing the approach carrier c x occupied at the observation before it (dev.governs(s, c) with st.lane_enters(c, i), or dev.governs(s, i)) displayed circular_red together with at least one green_arrow(dir) (read with since: occupancy of i since the entry under that display). The duty does not apply where a node of paragraph (b) applies (NRS_484B_307_9b_o1 to _o4, ruleApplies with x mapped to x).
obligation: Wherever x is moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance): for every pedestrian p (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) occupying a crosswalk w with st.entrance_of(w, c2) and st.lane_enters(c2, i) for some carrier c2, and every member z of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic other than x occupying i, not both prim.closest_approach_within(x, ·) over p.conflict_time_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance(x, ·) over that horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. With no such party present the duty is met.

narrowings.why: 'lawfully within' and 'lawfully using' are read as within and using: the lawfulness of the other road user's own conduct is the verdict of rules this corpus does not state, so every pedestrian in an adjacent crosswalk and every other member of traffic in the intersection is yielded to. The yield is judged while x crosses the intersection it entered under the arrow.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car enters on circular_red with green_arrow(left) and turns left while a pedestrian walks in the crosswalk marking the entrance of the cross street's approach; while the car moves their predicted closest approach within the horizon is below the conflict clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The car halts inside the intersection until the pedestrian has cleared and turns with no predicted conflict while it moves.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The car enters on circular_green and turns left.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car turns on the arrow while a pedestrian on a crosswalk at the intersection is in predicted conflict with it; the source does not record which approach the crosswalk marks.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car enters on red with a green left arrow and turns left with no other road user in the scene.
